segments.text_en: God Plays Dice. A century ago, physicists discovered that the universe is not a clockwork — it is a casino. This is the story of how certainty died, and what replaced it.
segments.text_ko: 신은 주사위를 던진다. 백 년 전, 물리학자들은 우주가 시계태엽이 아니라 카지노라는 사실을 발견했다. 확실성이 죽고, 그 자리를 차지한 것의 이야기.

segments.text_en: The experiment that shattered reality. Why this matters. Chapter 0 In 1801, Thomas Young passed light through two narrow slits and saw something impossible: an interference pattern — proof that light is a wave. A century later, physicists repeated the experiment firing one photon at a time . Each photon landed as a single dot. But as thousands accumulated, the interference pattern emerged again. A single particle, somehow interfering with itself . Things got stranger: when they placed a detector at one slit to see which way the photon went, the pattern vanished. Observation itself changed the outcome. photons: 0 "If you think you understand quantum mechanics, you don't understand quantum mechanics." — Richard Feynman The double-slit experiment is not just a curious lab trick.
segments.text_ko: 현실을 산산조각 낸 실험. 왜 이것이 중요한가. 제0장 In 1801, Thomas Young passed light through two narrow slits and saw something impossible: an interference pattern — proof that light is a wave. 광자: 0 "양자역학을 이해했다고 생각한다면, 양자역학을 이해하지 못한 것이다." — 리처드 파인만 The double-slit experiment is not just a curious lab trick.

segments.text_en: The universe was perfect. Two demons, two worldviews. What went wrong?. Chapter 1 For two hundred years, physics was a triumph of certainty. Newton's laws could predict the motion of every planet, every cannonball, every grain of sand — if you knew the starting conditions. The universe was a clockwork machine , and the laws of physics were its gears. drag a ball and release to shoot — watch perfect Newtonian mechanics Every collision obeys conservation of momentum and energy exactly. No surprises. No randomness. Given the positions and velocities of every particle in the universe, the entire future is already determined.
segments.text_ko: 우주는 완벽 했다. 두 악마, 두 세계관. 무엇이 잘못되었는가?. 제1장 For two hundred years, physics was a triumph of certainty. 공을 드래그하고 놓아 발사하세요 — 완벽한 뉴턴 역학 Every collision obeys conservation of momentum and energy exactly. "An intellect which at a certain moment would know all forces… and all positions of all items of which nature is composed — nothing would be uncertain, and the future just like the past would be present before its eyes." — 피에르-시몽 라플라스, 1814 This hypothetical being — 라플라스's demon — could, in principle, compute the future of the entire cosmos from a single snapshot. 라플라스's demon knows everything and computes the future.

segments.text_en: The oven that broke physics. A reluctant revolutionary and a bold one. Chapter 2 In 1859, Gustav Kirchhoff posed a challenge: determine the spectrum of light emitted by a heated cavity. By the 1890s, experimentalists had mapped the curve precisely. But no theory could explain it. Classical physics made a terrifying prediction. The Rayleigh–Jeans law — derived honestly from Maxwell's electromagnetism and Boltzmann's thermodynamics — said that the energy radiated should grow without bound at high frequencies. A warm oven should emit infinite energy in the ultraviolet. This was absurd. The physicist Paul Ehrenfest gave it a name: the ultraviolet catastrophe . A heated cavity. Photons bounce inside, reaching thermal equilibrium.
segments.text_ko: 물리학을 깨뜨린 오븐. 마지못한 혁명가와 대담한 혁명가. 제2장 In 1859, Gustav 키르히호프 posed a challenge: determine the spectrum of light emitted by a heated cavity. "Briefly summarized, what I did can be described as simply an act of desperation." — 막스 플랑크, R.W. Wood에게 보낸 편지, 1931 Five years later, a young patent clerk in Bern took 플랑크's quanta seriously. 플랑크 introduced quanta as a mathematical trick and spent years trying to take it back.

segments.text_en: The more you know, the less you know. The vacuum is not empty. Chapter 3 Imagine trying to locate an electron. You shine light on it. But light carries momentum — to see something small, you need short-wavelength (high-energy) light, which kicks the electron unpredictably. Use gentle long-wavelength light, and you cannot see where it is. This was Heisenberg's gamma-ray microscope thought experiment, published in 1927. But the uncertainty principle goes deeper than clumsy measurements. It is not that we disturb the particle by looking. The particle genuinely does not have a definite position and momentum simultaneously. The wave function — the mathematical object that describes a quantum particle — simply cannot be both narrow in position and narrow in momentum at the same time.
segments.text_ko: 더 많이 알수록, 더 적게 알게 된다. 진공은 비어 있지 않다. 제3장 Imagine trying to locate an electron. "The more precisely the position is determined, the less precisely the momentum is known in this instant, and vice versa." — 베르너 하이젠베르크, 1927 A quantum particle confined to a box. "신은 우주와 주사위 놀이를 하지 않는다." — 알베르트 아인슈타인 "아인슈타인, 신에게 이래라저래라 하지 마시오." — 닐스 보어의 유명한 대답 The uncertainty principle applies to all conjugate pairs — including energy and time.

segments.text_en: A coin that is both. The hard problem of quantum mechanics. Chapter 4 Imagine flipping a coin that is, genuinely, both heads and tails at once — not because you haven't looked, but because it has no single value until you do. A quantum particle in a superposition does not simply have an unknown state. It exists in all possible states simultaneously. When we measure, the superposition collapses to a single definite outcome. In 1922, Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach sent silver atoms through an inhomogeneous magnetic field. Classically, the atoms should have spread into a continuous smear. Instead, they split into exactly two beams — spin up and spin down. Nature gives only discrete answers. ↑ 0 ↓ 0 Silver atoms enter a magnetic field. Classically, they should spread smoothly.
segments.text_ko: 동시에 앞면이자 뒷면 인 동전. 양자역학의 난제. 제4장 Imagine flipping a coin that is, genuinely, both heads and tails at once — not because you haven't looked, but because it has no single value until you do. "양자역학을 이해하는 사람은 아무도 없다." — 리처드 파인만, 물리 법칙의 특성 , 1965 Erwin 슈뢰딩거 devised his famous thought experiment in 1935 — not to celebrate quantum weirdness, but to ridicule it . A cat is penned up in a steel chamber…" — 에르빈 슈뢰딩거, 1935 Eugene Wigner pushed this further with Wigner's friend : if a physicist inside a lab measures the cat, they see a definite result. The measurement problem is sometimes called the "hard problem" of physics, by analogy with the hard problem of consciousness.

segments.text_en: Spooky action at a distance. The 2022 Nobel Prize. Chapter 5 In May 1935, Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen published a paper with an innocent title and an explosive argument. Two particles, once entangled, remain correlated no matter how far apart. Measure one — the other's state is instantly determined. Einstein saw only two options: either information travels faster than light (impossible), or the particles always "knew" their values in advance through hidden variables . He concluded quantum mechanics must be incomplete. Bohr's response, published months later, was characteristically opaque. He argued that one cannot speak of the properties of a particle independently of the measurement context. Einstein was unconvinced.
segments.text_ko: 으스스한 원격 작용. 2022년 노벨상. 제5장 In May 1935, Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen published a paper with an innocent title and an explosive argument. Alice 입자 측정 — and watch Bob's instantly resolve to the correlated state, no matter the distance. "I cannot seriously believe in [quantum mechanics] because the theory cannot be reconciled with the idea that physics should represent a reality in time and space, free from spooky actions at a distance." — 알베르트 아인슈타인, 막스 보른에게 보낸 편지, 1947 test. 홀데인 (양자 맥락에서 자주 인용) There is one remaining loophole: superdeterminism .

segments.text_en: What does it all mean ?. Thought experiment: quantum teleportation. Why it matters. Thought experiment: the quantum eraser. The future of the debate. Chapter 6 Quantum mechanics is, by any measure, the most successful theory in the history of science. It predicts the behavior of atoms, molecules, semiconductors, lasers, and nuclear reactions with staggering accuracy. But after a century, physicists still cannot agree on what the theory says about reality . The fight began at the fifth Solvay Conference in October 1927 — perhaps the most extraordinary gathering of minds in history. Twenty-nine physicists, seventeen of whom were or would become Nobel laureates, met in Brussels to discuss the newly born quantum theory. Einstein and Bohr squared off.
segments.text_ko: 이 모든 것은 무엇을 의미 하는가?. 사고 실험: 양자 텔레포테이션. 사고 실험: 양자 지우개. 논쟁의 미래. 제6장 "아무도 보지 않을 때 달은 거기 있는가?" — 아브라함 파이스, 코펜하겐 해석에 대한 아인슈타인의 반론을 빗대어 A century later, the debate is unresolved.
